newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Road deaths dominate EU's transport cost table.
newsitem.headline: Road deaths dominate EU's transport cost table.

text.p: Death, injury and damage from road crashes make up all but three percent of the 166-billion-Ecu ($198 billion) annual bill for EU transport accidents, a European safety lobby said on Wednesday.
"Around 97 percent of all socio-economic costs for transport accidents within the EU are made in road transport," the European Transport Safety Council (ETSC) said in a statement.

"This is mainly due to the large share of road transport compared to other modes and the much higher risk levels in road transport," it said, adding that about 70 percent of EU freight and 88 percent of passenger traffic went by road.
An ETSC report put the EU death toll from transport accidents at 46,666 people in 1995, with 45,000 killed on the road, 1,300 on the railways, 186 in aviation and 180 in water transport.
It calculated the cost of accidents in rail, air and waterways transport at 2.74 billion Ecus, 500 million Ecus and 1.78 billion Ecus respectively.
"It is clear that higher priority should be given to road safety in EU and member states' transport investments," said ETSC executive director Jeanne Breen.
"The enormous socio-economic costs of road accidents and the largely avoidable premature loss of life needs urgent attention at national and international level," she added.
The study itself acknowledged difficulties in compiling accident cost data for non-road incidents, describing its estimates for these modes as "necessarily crude and based on many assumptions".

It said its figures for potential savings should be used to argue the economic case for improved road safety features and urged the inclusion of cost estimates for unreported accidents in such calculations.
